ai-cyber-security.name: AI for Cyber Security
ai-cyber-security.description: Comprehensive academic study engine covering machine learning, deep learning, behavioral biometrics, threat detection, and fraud prevention for digital systems.
learningObjectives: Explain fundamental cybersecurity principles, the CIA triad, and the evolution of AI from expert systems to deep learning.
Master the AI cybersecurity arsenal: classification, regression, dimensionality reduction, clustering, video anomaly analysis, NLP, and large-scale image processing.
Formulate and implement threat detection models using Perceptron, SVM, Logistic Regression, Decision Trees, Naive Bayes, and NLP pipelines.
Engineer proactive identity and asset defense systems using authentication abuse prevention, account reputation scoring, keystroke dynamics, and facial biometrics.
Architect real-time fraud prevention engines using ensemble methods (Bagging vs Boosting), exploratory data analysis, and rigorous statistical evaluation metrics.
courseOutcomes: CO1: Apply AI techniques, including expert systems and data mining, to enhance cybersecurity measures.
CO2: Implement classification, regression, and NLP techniques for analyzing cybersecurity threats and social media risks.
CO3: Utilize AI models like Perceptrons, SVMs, and decision trees for detecting spam, phishing, and cyber threats.
CO4: Apply AI-driven authentication methods, including keystroke dynamics and facial recognition, for security enhancement.
CO5: Leverage machine learning algorithms, ensemble techniques, and statistical metrics for fraud detection and prevention.

cyber-forensics.name: Cyber Forensics
cyber-forensics.description: Comprehensive digital forensics curriculum connecting evidence preservation, file systems, memory and network analysis, specialized devices, and defensible reporting through an interactive bank cyberattack investigation.
learningObjectives: Understand digital forensic principles, legal compliance, Section 65B certification, Chain of Custody, and write-blocked dead/live acquisition.
Analyze storage structures (FAT, NTFS, ext4), deleted file recovery, slack space, data carving using magic bytes, and Windows OS execution artifacts.
Execute volatile memory triage, Volatility 3 rootkit analysis, RFC 3227 order of volatility, event log correlation, and Super Timeline generation.
Examine specialized endpoints, Android vs iOS security sandboxing, mobile extraction tiers (logical/FS/physical), SQLite database parsing, and IoT smart CCTV forensics.
Master large-scale case management (EDRM), court-admissible forensic report writing, expert witness testimony ethics, and NIST CFTT tool validation.
courseOutcomes: CO1: Acquire and preserve digital evidence following RFC 3227 and statutory legal compliance standards.
CO2: Recover deleted data and analyze operating system execution artifacts (Registry, Prefetch, LNK, Shellbags).
CO3: Conduct live volatile memory triage using Volatility 3 and correlate multi-source logs into a normalized UTC Super Timeline.
CO4: Extract and evaluate smartphone SQLite databases, geolocation telemetry, and embedded IoT hardware evidence.
CO5: Produce court-defensible forensic reports and defend analytical findings under expert witness cross-examination standards.
